title: algebraic residue field extension closed point fibre
conclusions: x closed in fibre X_s
If s closed in S then x closed in X
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
If $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$
is an algebraic field extension, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is a closed point of its fibre, and
\item if in addition $s$ is a closed point of $S$, then
$x$ is a closed point of $X$.
\end{enumerate}

title: closed point fibre locally finite type
conclusions: x closed in scheme fibre X_s iff κ(x)/κ(s) finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Then $x$ is a closed point of its fibre
if and only if $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is
a finite field extension.

title: base change closed point fibre locally finite type
explicit_hypotheses: x'∈X' mapping to x∈X closed in X_{f(x)}
conclusions: x' closed in X'_{f'(x')}
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $g : S' \to S$ be any morphism. Denote $f' : X' \to S'$ the base change.
If $x' \in X'$ maps to a point $x \in X$ which is closed in $X_{f(x)}$
then $x'$ is closed in $X'_{f'(x')}$.

title: residue field quasi finite
conclusions: κ(x)/κ(s) finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
If $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then the residue field
extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite.

title: quasi finite at point characterize
equivalent_conditions: x closed in X_s with no other point of X_s specializing to x
For every eligible affine U=Spec(A), V=Spec(R), ring map R→A quasi-finite at prime corresponding to x
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
Let $X_s$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$.
\item The point $x$ is isolated in $X_s$.
\item The point $x$ is closed in $X_s$
and there is no point $x' \in X_s$, $x' \not = x$
which specializes to $x$.
\item For any pair of affine opens
$\Spec(A) = U \subset X$, $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with
$f(U) \subset V$ and $x \in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q \subset A$
the ring map $R \to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$.
\end{enumerate}

title: finite fibre
conclusions: X_s has finite discrete underlying topological space
f quasi-finite at each x above s
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $s \in S$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite type, and
\item $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set.
\end{enumerate}
Then $X_s$ is a finite discrete topological space, and
$f$ is quasi-finite at each point of $X$ lying over $s$.

title: locally quasi finite fibres
equivalent_conditions: Each fibre X_s has discrete underlying topological space
For every field k and Spec(k)→S the base-change X_k has discrete underlying topology
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally quasi-finite,
\item for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a discrete topological space, and
\item for every morphism $\Spec(k) \to S$ where $k$ is a field
the base change $X_k$ has an underlying discrete topological space.
\end{enumerate}

title: quasi finite locally quasi compact
conclusions: f quasi-finite iff f locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Then $f$ is quasi-finite if and only if $f$ is
locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact.

title: quasi finite
conclusions: f quasi-finite iff f locally of finite type, quasi-compact and each fibre finite

title: locally quasi finite characterize
conclusions: When equivalent conditions hold, restrictions f|_U:U→V to any compatible opens are locally quasi-finite
equivalent_conditions: Every eligible affine pair U⊆X, V⊆S induces quasi-finite ring map O_S(V)→O_X(U)
An open-cover test of locally quasi-finite U_i→V_j holds
An affine-cover test of quasi-finite ring maps O_S(V_j)→O_X(U_i) holds
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is locally quasi-finite.
\item For every pair of affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is quasi-finite.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is locally quasi-finite.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
quasi-finite, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is locally quasi-finite then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally quasi-finite.

title: composition quasi finite
conclusions: composite locally quasi-finite (respectively quasi-finite)
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\) be morphisms of schemes. If both are locally quasi-finite, then \(g\circ f\) is locally quasi-finite; if both are quasi-finite, then \(g\circ f\) is quasi-finite.

title: base change quasi finite
conclusions: Quasi-finite point locus U' of f' equals (g')^{-1}(U), where U is the quasi-finite point locus of f
Base changes of locally quasi-finite maps are locally quasi-finite
Base changes of quasi-finite maps are quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Denote $f' : X' \to S'$ the base change of $f$ by $g$
and denote $g' : X' \to X$ the projection.
Assume $X$ is locally of finite type over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $U \subset X$ (resp.\ $U' \subset X'$)
be the set of points where $f$ (resp.\ $f'$) is quasi-finite.
Then $U' = U \times_S S' = (g')^{-1}(U)$.
\item The base change of a locally quasi-finite morphism is
locally quasi-finite.
\item The base change of a quasi-finite morphism is
quasi-finite.
\end{enumerate}
unresolved_context: The equality of quasi-finite loci involves scheme-theoretic U×_S S' and topological inverse image; both meanings should be preserved

title: quasi finite at a finite number of points
conclusions: Finitely many x∈X_s at which f is quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes of finite type.
Let $s \in S$. There are at most finitely many points
of $X$ lying over $s$ at which $f$ is quasi-finite.

title: monomorphism loc finite type loc quasi finite
explicit_hypotheses: f locally of finite type and monomorphism
conclusions: f separated
f locally quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
If $f$ is locally of finite type and a monomorphism, then $f$
is separated and locally quasi-finite.

title: immersion locally quasi finite
conclusions: f locally quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex: Every immersion \(f:X\to Y\) of schemes is locally quasi-finite.

title: permanence quasi finite
conclusions: If X→S quasi-finite at x then X→Y quasi-finite at x
If X→S locally quasi-finite then X→Y locally quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Let $x \in X$. If $X \to S$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then
$X \to Y$ is quasi-finite at $x$.
If $X$ is locally quasi-finite over $S$, then $X \to Y$
is locally quasi-finite.

title: quasi finite local source
conclusions: g locally quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes.
If $f$ is surjective, $g \circ f$ locally quasi-finite, and
$g$ locally of finite type, then $g : Y \to S$  is locally quasi-finite.
